description: THE MB-4 OPT-IN DISJOINT-UNION GOLDEN (docs/design/multi-body.md §MB-4): a `boolean` union of two NON-TOUCHING bodies with `allow_disjoint: true` produces ONE multi-lump body (a Compound of the two disjoint lumps), NOT a `boolean_disjoint` error. Five features: (1) a 20x20 mm square on the XY origin datum at x,y in [0,20]; (2) extrude add 20 mm up -> body A, a 20x20x20 cube (merge absent -> True, first body); (3) a second 20x20 mm square on the SAME XY datum at x in [30,50] (a 10 mm gap from A); (4) extrude add 20 mm up with merge=FALSE -> body B, a SECOND 20x20x20 cube; (5) a `boolean` union, target=extrude A / tool=extrude B, with allow_disjoint=true. Because A and B do not touch, the OCCT fuse yields TWO disjoint solids; allow_disjoint keeps them as ONE multi-lump body (a lump-sorted Compound) under the target's identity slot, and the tool body is consumed. The part ends with a SINGLE bodies-entry that is a two-lump Compound -- so the same analytic numbers as the MB-0 `multibody-two-disjoint-boxes` golden (16000 mm^3, shells=2, 12 faces / 24 edges), but reached via a boolean into ONE body, measured through the single-body measure path (measure_shape over the Compound: GProp integration + .shells() across both lumps). Locks MB-4a end to end: (a) the relaxed >1-solid branch of boolean_bodies returns a lump-sorted Compound; (b) the widened EvaluationState.bodies holds a BodyShape; (c) the flattened part roll-up tessellates the Compound deterministically; (d) byte-identical GLB across an interpreter restart + STEP multi-solid round-trip.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). The geometry is identical to the MB-0 `multibody-two-disjoint-boxes` golden -- two axis-aligned 20x20x20 cubes, A at x,y in [0,20] and B at x in [30,50], y in [0,20], both z in [0,20], with a 10 mm gap in x -- but here the two lumps are combined into ONE body by a `boolean` union with allow_disjoint=true, rather than left as two bodies. The lumps are DISJOINT (share no face/edge/vertex), so every analytic quantity is identical to the two-body case.

volume = A + B = 8000 + 8000 = 16000 mm^3 exactly (disjoint, so no overlap subtraction). Measured deviation vs analytic: ~4e-12 mm^3 (a couple of ulp at the 1.6e4 scale, the OCCT fuse of non-touching bodies is an exact lump union).
surface_area = 2 cubes * 6 faces * (20*20 = 400) = 4800 mm^2. Every face of both lumps is external (they do not touch), so allow_disjoint keeps all 12 faces. Measured deviation: ~1e-12 mm^2.

centroid = (25, 10, 10) mm: lump A (V=8000, centroid (10,10,10)) and lump B (V=8000, centroid (40,10,10)) give x = (8000*10 + 8000*40)/16000 = 25.0; y = z = 10 by symmetry. Measured over the single Compound by GProp (VolumeProperties CentreOfMass), not re-meshed. Measured deviation: x exactly 25.0, z within 2e-15, y within 5e-15 (GProp ulp).

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[50,20,20]: the union of A's AABB [0,0,0]..[20,20,20] and B's AABB [30,0,0]..[50,20,20]. Exact prisms of axis-aligned boxes, so all six bounds are EXACT (measured deviation 0.0).

topology = 12 faces, 24 edges, 2 SHELLS: each lump has 6 faces / 12 edges / 1 closed shell, counted across the Compound by shape.faces()/edges()/shells(). shells=2 is the load-bearing MB-4 assertion: the boolean produced a genuinely two-lump body (allow_disjoint kept it as one body rather than erroring), so the shell count is 2 -- distinct from the single-connected boolean goldens' shells=1. Per-lump Euler-Poincare cross-check: V - E + F = 8 - 12 + 6 = 2 = 2*(1-0), a valid closed manifold solid; the body is two such shells.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, faceted per-face normals, no vertex sharing across faces -- the box-golden convention): each lump face is a planar quad -> 4 vertices / 2 triangles; 6 faces per lump = 24 vertices / 12 triangles; two lumps = 48 vertices / 24 triangles. glb_stats sums over the flattened Compound's two lump meshes.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). This is TWO disjoint planar B-reps kept as one Compound body by an allow_disjoint boolean union (OCCT BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse of non-touching solids); its properties come from a single GProp integration over the Compound plus a .shells() count. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-18, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume ~4e-12 mm^3, surface_area ~1e-12 mm^2, bounding_box exactly 0.0 on all six bounds, centroid x exact and y/z <= 5e-15 mm. Documented ceiling 1e-9 (matching the sibling multibody-two-disjoint-boxes golden) is ~250x the observed worst case (~4e-12, volume), headroom for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm at model scale). The solver contributes zero error by construction (both squares are shape-pinned, under-constrained only in whole-sketch position -> planegcs returns the drawn positions bitwise; solved == input). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
